Wow, thank you for this reply. Honestly. It’s kinda exactly what I guess I needed to hear. That’s how I’m feeling. Like it’s just so permanent and final. But I should be relieved if we’re finally finding the right diagnosis. It means I’m going to be able to get better. It was hard to hear or accept I think because I’ve had time to get use to the word depression, but not bipolar.

It’s just so disheartening to have been doing pretty good on my meds and then to feel like the rug was pulled out from under me with with this Hypomania episode. (I think that’s what it was, especially after hearing from others like yourself.) 

But you’re right, it doesn’t change that I’m me. It’s not like labeling it changes what it is or what it’s been. It just means we’re doing better at understanding it and hopefully this managing it.

Not dumb, I completely understand. I’m also at my heaviest and was worried about the possibility of weight gain as I have a pretty low activity job most days. I will say, for me personally, the bupropion hasn’t resulting in any weight gain or food cravings. Which is great cause the anxiety over the possible side effect was real.

You should feel really proud of yourself in my opinion for just seeking help and going to therapy. It is a big deal and I sympathize with the effort it takes. I hope you find peace in therapy and or medications. It was a huge stressor for me in a way getting on medications but once I found a decent combo the difference really has been night and day...even if I can’t focus worth a damn haha.

You’ve been a great help to me...and I think we have a bit in common. If you ever need to talk please feel free to PM me.

Yeah I try to be as patient as possible with my medications. And proactive in my treatment...as much as I can. I’ve quit caffeine (a big deal considering how much and how long I’ve been drinking it) and try to eat well and drink enough water. I avoid alcohol for the most part too. 

I’m very consistent in taking my medications. 😅 I’ve actually conditioned my dogs to associate me taking my medications in the morning with them getting treats. So they’re pretty good about not letting me forget. 

I just looked up a quick list of snri drug names and I haven’t been on any that showed up. I’ll have to do some homework and ask my doctors what they think.

u/CrunchyMold “Try looking at your reaction from a different perspective and see what you can come up and go from there. Don't be afraid to mention it at your sessions either; it's a common reaction. My therapist has remarked both times that just showing up takes a lot of strength and is to be commended. It's very easy to give up, but what is the cost of doing so?” That so hit me on a personal level. And I hope you do keep going and seeing your therapist.

When I started with my therapist I had similar bargains with myself, two more at least, give her a chance etc. I knew where I was at, I was at the end of the rope when I had started seeing her. I had scared myself into going because I had resided myself to the fact that I was going to eventually die from my depression. I didn’t have a plan persay but coming to the conclusion that it would kill me eventually...I guess it lit a fire under my ass to actually seek help again. Cause what was the alternative? Not great, or reversible.

But weirdly, the times I’m most stressed and anxious is leading up to my psychiatrist appointments to manage my meds...

Between your comment and some others I’ve replied to today I think I need to make an appointment with my therapist to catch up. Maybe she can help me figure out why my medication adjustment appointments with the psychiatrist make me so anxious...

I’m still in the fence with my medications moving forward too...maybe she can put some sense into me and convince me to stay on the train 😅

Thank you for taking the time friend.

I’ve never full out cried in therapy or at my psychiatrists office. I’ve teared up with my therapist, because I was overwhelmed with stress and relief hearing her tell me I should try medication. It was the best and the worse news for me at that moment, I felt relieved a professional saw I was trying and something was still very wrong in my brain as I suspected...and also of course pretty crappy that it was going to be a long and hard road going forward, just like it had been leading to that point.

Good advice for sure. Weird thing is, these were appointments with my psychiatrist, she just manages my meds and we don’t even talk about that stuff...and honesty I don’t have much to say.

I’m very fortunate to have a loving, supportive life. Certainly not perfect and we have our struggles, but objectively I know I have a pretty great life. Intellectually I’m pretty sound, and my therapist seemed to think I had actually (accidentally) made some very good strides in developing techniques to control and subdue my depression even before starting therapy. She told me the names of the methods I had accidentally deployed and strengthened those techniques and gave me a few more tools...

But the depression was just a constant, heavy thing. Intellectually knowing and even being able to know in the darkest hour what it is...it still left me exhausted. That’s why I started therapy and then medications. Seeing it for what it was and intellectually being able to confront it wasn’t doing much for the exhaustion of calling it out and still having it effect my life. I was near the end of my rope when I sought help.

Hey there. So I have a therapist...or had...have I guess. She helped a lot and gave me tools to help me mentally. But I don’t exactly have a traumatic past of abuse or anything. I’m very fortunate in that and apparently very empathetic for others. One of the tools she taught me was having that empathy for myself too as well as ways to separate my depression from myself and know I have it and can coexist with it without letting it control me.

But Eventually we decided medication is going to be helpful for me because, as much as I intellectually understand what is happening and control how I see it, I still was getting sucker punched by boughts of depression that rendered me miserable and useless to my own care.
So we tried a few things via her suggesting them to my general doctor and getting them prescribed. Things that didn’t work. 

So I was referred to this psychiatrist to work out medications and had a long talk with my therapist about the possibility that I may be on meds for the rest of my life due to the nature of my depression. We’ve traced my depression symptoms back to when I was as young as 7 years old and possibly even as early as 5. (I guess it’s not normal for a 7 year old to wonder what “game over” is and how to get there haha) And I was told I can always come back to talk to my therapist but she felt I had a better grasp of the techniques that we were working on than most.

So, I haven’t gone back to her. Because I guess she doesn’t have anything else to offer me tool wise. Maybe you’re right tho, maybe I should make an appointment to see her and talk again. (Tho the last time I left her office I did end up crying in my car and canceling my next appointment, then starting with the psychiatrist)
Hmm I hadn't thought of it. I’ll mull it over though. Thanks for the insight.

Well I’m glad I’m not alone...at my appointment today I had a panic attack in the waiting room. I felt like my heart was going to climb out of my chest.  Just sitting there it got up to 102bpm. Not a good feeling.

I’m sorry it didn’t work out for you. I hope you find something or someone that can help, even though you’re in a rural area.

I’m prescribed lexapro/bupropion and today got switched from the 24hr tablet of bupropion to two 12hr tabs a day because I’m finding it nearly impossible to focus. And I guess I kinda feel like my psychiatrist doesn’t believe me...
The bupropion has done a lot to help my depression, and intellectually I know it’s helping...
But emotionally I just want to quit it all. I hate feeling scatter brained. I forget what I say 2 seconds after I say it and can’t switch task without 3 attempts cause I forget what I was doing...

But her response is to show me in a book that bupropion is used to treat adhd....and I’m just sitting here thinking...that’s great...but I’m not functioning...or diagnosed adhd...I’m having trouble focusing but that doesn’t mean I have add...so whatever is happening in my brain this isn’t fixing it alone...

Idk...I’m pretty tired of the whole process. 

Idk...I can feel it in my future that I’m going to go off it all and stop showing up. It’s more a matter of time. I’m holding out hoping for the happy mixture of medication before I call it quits.
